model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)
model_label: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (run on the component engine: revenue x cash-FFO margin less leasing/maintenance capex = AFFO available to common; discounted at the USD cost of equity; net debt NOT deducted)

historical_growth.eps_basis: Nareit FFO per diluted share, NOT GAAP EPS: FY2022 $1.58 -> FY2025 $1.76 (3yr, 3.7%); FY2020 $1.16 (COVID base, rent deferrals) -> FY2025 $1.76 (5yr, 8.7%); FY2019 $1.44 -> FY2025 $1.76 is 3.4%/yr across the COVID and rate cycles. FY2024 $1.65 and FY2025 $1.76 are verified against the Q4-25 release in this run; FY2019-FY2023 are Kimco's reported figures from earlier releases (FY2021 $1.38, FY2023 $1.57) and were not re-verified here. GAAP EPS (FY2020 $2.25 on the Albertsons gain, FY2022 $0.16, FY2025 $0.82) is gains-and-depreciation noise and its CAGR is meaningless.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: Total Nareit FFO in US$m: FY2022 ~976 (1.58 x 617.9m) -> FY2025 1,194.1 (3yr, 7.0%); FY2020 ~502 -> FY2025 1,194.1 (5yr, 18.9%; Weingarten Aug-2021 and RPT Jan-2024 all-stock mergers). AFFO is derived from the outlook-table bridge items that Kimco only tabulates from FY2025, so no AFFO CAGR is computable. Per-share FFO (3.7% 3yr) is the honest organic figure; the merger-driven total CAGRs are not used.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 FFO guidance (+4.0-4.5% on FY2025's $1.76, raised Aug-2026 after H1 +3.5% and Q2 +4.5%), the $75m signed-not-open ABR pipeline (400bp leased-to-economic spread) and 3.0-3.5% same-property NOI growth, fading toward the ~3.5% long-run per-share FFO record; the base path averages ~3.1% over FY2026-35. Equity CAGR is not used: Kimco's book equity is depreciated historical cost inflated by stock-funded mergers.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (13.2% 5yr) diverges from FFO-per-share CAGR (8.7% 5yr) and revenue CAGR (7.4% 3yr vs 3.0% 3yr equity) by more than 30%. The divergence is merger accounting (Weingarten +$3.9bn and RPT +$1.1bn of equity issued) and depreciation, not operating performance; growth is taken from the per-share FFO series and guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue and total-FFO CAGRs overstate organic growth: FY2020 is a COVID base and FY2021-24 include two all-stock mergers that grew the share count from 432m to 680m. Per-share FFO compounded 3.4-3.7%/yr. AFFO grew slower than FFO in FY2025 because leasing capex ($305m) ran ahead of the guided $275-300m as record leasing volumes (2.5m sq ft in Q2-26 alone) pulled TI/LC forward; the leased-to-economic occupancy spread (400bp, $75m ABR) is rent that the capex has already paid for but that has not yet commenced.

scenario_narratives.base: Kimco delivers the raised FY2026 guidance ($1.83-1.84 FFO per share, +4-4.5%) and then compounds FFO at 3-4% for three years as the $75m signed-not-open rent commences, same-property NOI grows 3-3.5% on contractual bumps and 40% new-lease spreads, and the Structured Investment Program adds 8-10% yields, before fading to a CPI-like 2.5%. Leasing and maintenance capex stays ~12.5-13% of revenue, so AFFO (~$1.34/share in FY2026E) covers the $1.12 dividend 1.2x and the retained ~$150m funds the redevelopment pipeline. No cap-rate compression and no discount-rate relief are assumed: the value is the AFFO stream capitalised at a 9% USD cost of equity, roughly what the current price already implies.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FY2025 pattern (guided $1.70-1.72, delivered $1.76) repeats; small-shop occupancy closes the gap to Regency and Federal, credit loss holds at the 55bp low end, the Fed easing cycle takes the 10-year toward 3.5% so the 2027-30 refinancing drift vanishes and shopping-center cap rates compress, and the Signature Series (10,000+ entitled residential units; The Milton sold at a 4.9% cap) plus the Structured Investment Program with its ROFO/ROFR pipeline deliver accretive external growth off the A-/A3 balance sheet. FFO grows 4-5% for five years, the cash-FFO margin expands 1.5pp and leasing capex normalises to 11.5% of revenue, so AFFO compounds ~5.5% and the exit is 17x.
scenario_narratives.bear: A consumer recession triggers a tenant-credit cycle: multiple national-chain bankruptcies (the Painted Tree rejections were the first) push credit loss above 100bp, occupancy slides from 96.4% to ~94%, and backfilling boxes needs 15% of revenue in TI and re-tenanting capital. Higher-for-longer rates lift refinancing costs ~200bp on the 2026-28 maturities and retail cap rates expand as in 2022-23, so Kimco sells assets to hold leverage inside 6x and the rent base shrinks. FFO stalls at 0.5-1.5% growth, the cash-FFO margin gives up 3pp, AFFO cover of the $1.12 dividend falls to ~1.0x, and the exit is 13.5x AFFO, the 2022-23 sector trough.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kimco is valued as a stream of AFFO available to common shareholders (Nareit FFO less non-cash GAAP revenues less leasing/maintenance capex, all on Kimco's own outlook-table definitions) capitalised at a 9.0% USD cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because the flow is already after $330m of interest and $30m of preferred dividends. GAAP net income, book-value growth and the XBRL free cash flow are all set aside: the first is depreciation-and-gains noise, the second is stock-funded merger accounting, and the third is pre-capex because real-estate capex is untagged. The base case is essentially the raised FY2026 guidance fading to CPI growth; it lands close to the current price, which means the market is capitalising Kimco at roughly a 9% cost of equity for ~3% growth -- fair, not cheap. The dividend ($1.12, 5.0% yield) is 84% of FY2026E AFFO, so the retained cash just covers the redevelopment budget; growth beyond CPI depends on recycling and the structured-investment pipeline being accretive.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: every 50bp on the cost of equity moves the base value ~8-9% because the terminal value is roughly half of it; the price already implies ~8.5-9%.

Capex bridge: FFO-to-AFFO leakage of $335-355m/yr (leasing/maintenance capex plus non-cash revenues) is ~28% of FFO. Kimco's definition is broader than sell-side 'recurring' AFFO; a street AFFO of ~$1.55 would put the same 9% capitalisation ~15% higher, and a bear-case 15% capex ratio takes it ~10% lower.
Refinancing: $8.7bn of consolidated debt plus ~$1.1bn pro-rata JV debt; 2026-28 maturities refinance ~150bp above their coupons, and interest + preferred is guided to rise $7-11m in FY2026 alone.
Tenant credit: TJX, Home Depot, Albertsons, Ross, Amazon/Whole Foods, Kroger and Walmart are ~20% of ABR; a bankruptcy wave in off-price or discount would hit occupancy, credit loss and TI at once.
Revenue is the driver line, not the valued flow: dispositions or a shift in the JV/structured-investment mix can move the cash-FFO margin without changing FFO.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 19.76-26.65.
data_sources.financials: KIM Metrics CSV / core_metrics (SEC XBRL companyfacts, CIK 879101: revenue, net income, D&A, SBC, equity-award taxes, buybacks, notes and mortgages payable, cash, shares); Q4-25 earnings release (8-K 12-Feb-2026 Ex.99.1: FY2025 FFO reconciliation $1,194.1m / $1.76, FY2025 outlook-table actuals for non-cash revenues $62m and leasing/maintenance capex $305m, initial FY2026 outlook); Q2-26 earnings release (8-K 4-Aug-2026 Ex.99.1: H1-26 FFO $620.4m, raised FY2026 outlook and assumptions, 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, FFO share table); 8-K 15-Jun-2026 (3.50% exchangeable notes due 2031, $32.36 exchange price); FY2025 10-K (20-Feb-2026).
data_sources.qualitative: KIM_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): business model, tenant concentration, occupancy, guidance, risk register, peer set.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 total revenues (Dec-25 year, US$m: revenues from rental properties, net 2,121.4 + management and other fee income 18.7; 10-K FY2025 / Q4-25 release). Revenue is the DRIVER line only. The flow that is valued is Nareit FFO available to common shareholders (55.8% of revenue in FY2025, 54.6% in FY2024, 56.0% in H1 2026) less non-cash GAAP revenues and less leasing/maintenance capex, i.e. AFFO on Kimco's own outlook-table definitions. Revenue and FFO have moved together, so the growth path is applied to revenue and read as FFO growth.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30-Jun-2026: 670,245,777 common shares issued and outstanding (Q2-26 balance sheet) + 3.8m exchangeable OP units + 0.65m dilutive equity awards (Q2-26 FFO share table) = 674.7m. Convertible preferred (3.2m as-converted shares) is NOT added because its dividend is already deducted from the flow (FFO available to common is net of all preferred dividends). The $600m 3.50% exchangeable notes (18.5m shares at the $32.36 exchange price, net-share settled above principal) are anti-dilutive at the current price and excluded. Held FLAT: the $120m FY2025 and $105m H1-26 buybacks (4.1m shares at $25.38 alongside the exchangeable issue) are treated as offsetting SBC issuance and unit/preferred conversions, not as a net reduction.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow discounted is AFFO available to common, which is already AFTER consolidated interest expense (FY2025 $330.2m; FY2026 guided interest + preferred dividends $368-372m) and after preferred dividends ($30.3m FY2025). Deducting the $8,040m balance-sheet net debt (notes 8,308.0 + mortgages 431.6 - cash 699.2 at 30-Jun-2026) on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never capitalise a post-interest flow and then subtract net debt). total_debt and cash below are recorded for audit only. Consolidated net debt / FY2025 EBITDA ~5.7x; A-/A3 unsecured ratings; $2.7bn immediate liquidity at 30-Jun-2026 ($700m cash incl. restricted, undrawn $2.0bn revolver); the June-2026 $600m exchangeable issue prefunded 2026-27 maturities, which is why cash jumped from $212m to $699m.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 AFFO available to common (US$m): Nareit FFO available to common 1,194.1 less non-cash GAAP revenues 62 (straight-line rent, above/below-market rent amortisation, straight-line reimbursement income; Kimco FY2025 outlook-table actual) less leasing and maintenance capex 305 (tenant improvements/allowances, capitalised external leasing commissions, capitalised building improvements; same table) = 827.1, or $1.23 per diluted share. This is the owner flow the valuation capitalises. NOT the CSV free_cash_flow of 1,101.6 (OCF 1,120.0 less an $18.4m PP&E line: XBRL does not tag Kimco's real-estate capex, so that FCF is pre-capex) and NOT FFO itself. Redevelopment capex ($83m FY2025, $125-150m guided FY2026, includes The Chester mixed-use development at Westlake) is growth capital funded from AFFO retained after the dividend (FY2026E AFFO ~$906m less ~$752m common dividends leaves ~$150m, which is the redevelopment budget) and is what the growth path pays for.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 Nareit FFO available to the company's common shareholders, $1,194.1m, $1.76 per diluted FFO share (681.9m FFO-diluted shares incl. units and convertible preferred), +6.7% on FY2024's $1,112.1m / $1.65. Q4-25 release reconciliation: net income to common 554.4 - gains on sale 62.7 - JV gains 6.6 + RE depreciation 622.5 + JV depreciation 84.5 + impairments 9.5 - loan-loss recovery 1.4 - profit participation 0.1 - securities/derivative gains 2.3 - tax 0.8 - NCI 3.0. H1 2026 FFO 620.4 / $0.92 (+3.5%; +4.5% in Q2). GAAP net income (592.8 FY2025) carries $62.7m of property gains and ~$627m of depreciation on assets that appreciate, so it is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based compensation of $33.2m FY2025 ($34.9m FY2024, $33.1m FY2023; XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation) plus $12.1m of tax withholding on net-share settlement is EXPENSED inside G&A and therefore inside FFO; Nareit FFO does not add it back and neither does this model, so no second deduction is made and the equity awards it grants (0.65m dilutive) are in the share count. House and street bases coincide (band collapsed) because the street AFFO convention that adds SBC back (~$0.05/share) is not applied here.
inputs.interest_income_note: Mortgage and other financing income ($51.0m FY2025, $45-50m guided FY2026) from the Structured Investment Program is left inside FFO because the matching asset ($412.7m of mortgage and other financing receivables at 30-Jun-2026) is NOT added to the equity value: excluded-income/matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction. Interest on the $699m cash is immaterial.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 payments for repurchase of common stock $120.3m (3.1m shares in Q4-25 at $19.96 plus earlier); H1 2026 $105.2m (4.1m shares at $25.38 with the exchangeable notes). Not projected: shares held flat.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-28T20:04:07Z (NYSE regular close; Yahoo v8 chart meta; 52-week range 19.76-26.65)
inputs.dps_note: Quarterly common dividend raised 12% to $0.28 (Aug-2026; $1.12 annualised) from $0.25 in 2025 ($1.00 FY2025 paid) and $0.26 in H1 2026. FY2026 cash DPS = 0.26+0.26+0.28+0.28 = $1.08. $1.12 is 84% of FY2026E AFFO of ~$1.34 and 61% of FFO guidance; the retained ~$150m funds the redevelopment budget.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the USD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest and post-preferred and no net debt is deducted: US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% (Sep-2026) + 1.0 beta x 5.0% US ERP = 9.2%, rounded to 9.0% for a grocery-anchored (necessity retail) landlord with A-/A3 ratings and maturities laddered mostly beyond 2030; a 1.2 beta (KIM's post-COVID trailing beta) would give 10.2%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows and the exit multiple). Cross-check: at the current_price (inputs.price_as_of) the market capitalises FY2026E AFFO of ~$1.34 at a ~6.0% AFFO yield and FY2026 FFO guidance at ~12.3x, i.e. an implied cost of equity of ~8.5-9.0% for 2.5-3.0% growth -- the house rate sits at the top of what the price implies.
inputs.lease_treatment: Ground-lease operating lease liabilities ($119.2m at 30-Jun-2026) are inside FFO as rent expense ($8.2m H1-26); no separate lease charge and no lease liability in the (zero) net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests ($8.1m FY2025; $157.4m NCI equity at 30-Jun-2026, mostly consolidated JV partners and OP units) is already deducted before 'FFO available to common'. OP units (3.8m) are added to the share count; their distributions ($36k) are immaterial. Equity in income of unconsolidated JVs ($96.8m FY2025) and JV depreciation add-back ($84.5m) are inside FFO, so pro-rata JV debt (~$1.1bn) is charged through the JV's own interest, not as a bridge item.
inputs.notes: Model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity -- routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md REIT row (equity REIT; GAAP net income is depreciation-and-gains noise, EBITDA/EV multiples double-count the debt the flow already services, XBRL FCF is pre-capex because real-estate capex is untagged). Run on the Drivers/engine route, GPT.AX/CHC.AX precedent: revenue is the driver line, EBITDA margin = CASH FFO margin ((Nareit FFO available to common - non-cash GAAP revenues) / revenue; post-interest, post-preferred, post-NCI, post the trivial TRS tax), D&A = 0 (real-estate depreciation is added back in FFO), SBC = 0 (expensed inside FFO), capex = leasing and maintenance capex (the FFO-to-AFFO bridge on Kimco's own definition), cash tax = 0 (REIT; FY2025 income tax $1.0m is inside FFO), working capital = 0, net_debt = 0. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Price is the 28-Sep-2026 NYSE regular close, not an after-hours print. Balance sheet and share count are from the 30-Jun-2026 10-Q (4-Aug-2026), the latest filing; the FY2025 10-K (20-Feb-2026) and the Q4-25 and Q2-26 earnings releases (EDGAR 8-K Ex.99.1) supply the FFO reconciliations and outlook tables. Subsequent events noted, not modelled: July-2026 repurchase of 516,750 Class N convertible preferred for $33.3m (a $3.8m charge hits Q3-26 FFO), $127m of Costco-anchored dispositions and $109m of Florida acquisitions through 1031 exchanges (net neutral to the flow).
inputs.sanity_multiples_note: P/E, EV/EBITDA and net-debt multiples are not meaningful for this ticker: net income is after ~$627m of real-estate depreciation and the flow discounted is post-interest. Use price / FFO (12.3x FY2026 guidance) and price / AFFO (~16.8x FY2026E) against the shopping-center REIT peer set (REG, BRX, FRT, KRG).

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands a point under guidance (H1 is banked; the $3.8m Class N repurchase charge hits Q3). Then a consumer recession plus a tenant-credit cycle: a wave of Painted Tree / Big Lots / Party City-style bankruptcies takes credit loss back above 100bp and occupancy from 96.4% to ~94%, re-leasing spreads compress, and higher-for-longer rates (10-year back above 5%) push refinancing costs up ~200bp on the $1.0-1.5bn of 2026-28 maturities while retail cap rates expand as they did in 2022-23. Recycling turns net-negative as Kimco sells to hold leverage inside 6x. FFO stalls at 0.5-1.5% growth, below CPI.
bear.margin_rationale: Cash FFO margin gives up 3pp as bad-debt expense doubles, NOI margin deleverages on lower occupancy and interest expense grows faster than revenue for three years.
bear.capex_rationale: Backfilling rejected anchor and junior-anchor boxes needs heavy TI and demolition/re-tenanting capital (as in the 2018-20 Toys R Us / Sears cycle); leasing and maintenance capex rises to 15% of revenue and AFFO cover of the $1.12 dividend falls to ~1.0x by FY2028.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 1.5% = 13.5x binds just under the 14x cap (a 7.4% exit AFFO yield, where shopping-center REITs traded through the 2022-23 rate shock).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = the raised FFO guidance ($1.83-1.84, +4.0-4.5%; H1 revenue +4.4%, Q2 FFO/share +4.5%). FY2027 4.0% on the $75m signed-not-open ABR commencing (~3.5% of revenue), 3.0-3.5% same-property NOI (contractual bumps ~2.6% plus 40% new-lease spreads) and structured-investment income, net of ~$10-15m/yr of interest-expense drift as 2026-28 maturities refinance ~150bp above their coupons; then fades to 2.5% -- contractual escalators with no cap-rate compression and net-neutral capital recycling assumed.
base.margin_rationale: Cash FFO / revenue: FY2025 actual 52.9% (FFO 1,194.1 - non-cash revenues 62 = 1,132.1 on 2,140.1); FY2026E 53.4% (guided FFO ~1,245 - non-cash 48-53 = ~1,195 on ~2,236 revenue). Held ~53.5% thereafter: NOI margin lifts from small-shop lease-up and $75m of SNO commencements are offset by interest-expense drift on the $8.7bn debt stack (guided interest + preferred $368-372m FY2026 vs $361m FY2025) and G&A growth. This is post-interest, post-preferred, post-NCI.
base.capex_rationale: Leasing and maintenance capex (the FFO-to-AFFO bridge: TI/allowances, capitalised leasing commissions, capitalised building improvements) at 12.9% of revenue in FY2026 = the $275-300m guidance midpoint on ~$2,236m revenue (FY2025 actual $305m = 14.3%, elevated by record leasing volume; H1-26 $115m run-rate is below guidance). Fades to 12.5% as the 400bp leased-to-economic spread closes and leasing volume normalises from the 2025-26 peak. Gives FY2026E AFFO ~$906m / $1.34 per share, 1.20x cover of the $1.12 annualised dividend. Redevelopment capex ($125-150m) is growth capital funded from the retained ~$150m and is excluded.
base.tax_rationale: Zero: REIT flow-through. The taxable REIT subsidiary's income tax ($1.0m FY2025, $0.8m H1-25) is already inside FFO.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 2.5% = 15.8x terminal AFFO (a 6.3% AFFO yield, ~5.0% implied FFO yield after the capex bridge) binds below the 18x cap. KIM trades at ~16.8x FY2026E AFFO today; shopping-center REIT peers 15-19x.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands at or above the top of the raised range as it did in FY2025 (initial $1.70-1.72, delivered $1.76); small-shop occupancy closes the gap to Regency/Federal (92.9% -> 94%+), the $75m SNO pipeline commences on schedule, credit loss stays at the 55bp low end, the Fed easing cycle takes the 10-year toward 3.5% so refinancing drift disappears and cap rates compress, and the Signature Series (10,000+ entitled residential units, The Milton sold at a 4.9% cap) plus the Structured Investment Program (8-10% yields with ROFO/ROFR on the underlying centers) add accretive external growth on the A-/A3 balance sheet.
bull.margin_rationale: Cash FFO margin drifts up 1.5pp as NOI margin expands with occupancy (fixed-cost operating leverage at 97%+ economic occupancy) and lower rates cut the refinancing cost of the 2027-30 maturities.
bull.capex_rationale: Leasing capex normalises toward the pre-2024 ratio (~11.5% of revenue) once the record leasing wave of 2025-26 has been paid for and renewals (6% spreads, low TI) dominate the roll.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 3.0% = 17.2x, inside the 18x cap. Same 9.0% cost of equity as base: the bull case is better flows and a lower capex bridge, not a cheaper discount rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: the Analysis JSON rates interest-rate sensitivity moderate-to-high, cap-rate expansion and consumer-spending risk moderate, and ~55% of the base value sits in a terminal multiple that the 2022-23 rate shock compressed to ~13x; tenant bankruptcies (Painted Tree) are already showing in 2026 occupancy. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs rates, small-shop lease-up, credit loss and the mixed-use pipeline to all go right at once. Base 50%: guidance has been raised twice with H1 banked, 96.4% occupancy is a record, and grocery-anchored rent is contractual income with limited new supply.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
